On one of the buildkite builds, I noticed that the MPI run fail even though the build did not throw an error. See https://buildkite.com/clima/climaland-ci/builds/11774#01a209e8-a352-45cf-8cd9-600f20d449fa.

`solve!` catches the error but only logs it. This results in the build succeeding. To fix this, `solve!` throws an error after closing the output writers and NetCDF files. To fix the MPI run, the default ODE algorithm is used.
title: Fix Global Run CPU MPI run

body:
When water or ice fills soil pores, the model keeps the O₂ of the layer while its effective porosity `θ_a + β_O₂ θ_l` shrinks. The O₂ fraction of the soil air, `so2`, then rises above the atmospheric 0.21. It rises about 12-fold when soil at θ_l = 0.25 saturates.

Gas barely diffuses through full pores, so the excess stays. The soil has no O₂ source. Physically, the displaced air and the O₂ that freezing water rejects leave the soil.

This PR releases the O₂ above the atmospheric concentration over one hour (`o2_release_rate`). The atmospheric concentration is taken at the air temperature, as in the top boundary condition. The column total is kept as a flux to the atmosphere, `o2_release_flux`, so O₂ mass is conserved. CO₂ is unchanged.

Column with no respiration and O₂ starting at 0.21; the soil below 0.5 m fills with water between day 1 and day 2:

| `so2` at 1.05 m | day 1 | day 2 | day 3 | day 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 0.210 | 2.58 | 2.58 | 2.58 |
| after | 0.210 | 0.31 | 0.210 | 0.210 |

The release is one-sided, so layers that diffusion reaches slowly settle at the concentration of the warmest air. With air at 263 ± 10 K over soil at 275 K, the daily mean `so2` at 2 m after 30 days is 0.211 instead of 0.219. Removing this would need diffusion of the O₂ mole fraction rather than its mass concentration.

This PR is stacked on #1984.

Tests:
- a unit test of `o2_release_rate`;
- in `saturation_stability_test.jl`, a saturated column holding ten times the atmospheric O₂. It checks the release, the O₂ tendency and the surface flux, and that nothing is released at the atmospheric concentration.

body:
The soil CO₂ and O₂ diffusivities (Ryan et al. 2018, after Moldrup et al. 2004) use `θ_a100`, the **air-filled** porosity at a matric potential of −100 cm H₂O. Ryan et al. (2018, Table 1) give 18.16 %, the value hard-coded before #690.

Since #690, `PrognosticMet` and `PrescribedMet` have computed `S(ψ = −1 m)(ν − θ_r) + θ_r`, which is the **water** content there. This PR computes the air content, `(ν − θ_r)(1 − S(ψ = −1 m))`, in `air_filled_porosity_100cm`, which both constructors now use. It also corrects "~10 Pa" to "~10 kPa" in the docstrings and adds the formula to the DAMM docs.

## Before / after

Default ROSETTA soil parameters, surface layer, weighted by area. These are computed offline with the model's formulas.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `θ_a100`, median (10–90 %) | 0.36 (0.24–0.46) | 0.10 (0.06–0.16) |
| Land where D exceeds the open-air diffusivity D0 | ~2.4 % (Sahara up to ~80 × D0) | 0 % |
| D_before / D_after, p10 / p50 / p90 | 0.54 / 0.93 / 1.17 | |

For most soils, D changes little. Coarse soils had D above D0, which soil cannot produce, and clays had D too low.

Respiration changes through the O₂ supply (`D_o2`). The calibrated soil-CO₂ parameters and the SOC spin-ups were tuned with the old diffusivity. The long run on this PR shows the effect on Rh, ER and NEE.

## Question for review: the ratio cap

`gas_diffusivity_in_soil` caps `θ_a / θ_a100` at 5 (#1714). With the old `θ_a100`, the cap binds on ≤ 0.2 % of land. With the new value, it binds in dry, fine-textured soils:

| Surface dried to ψ = | −15 m | −150 m | −10⁴ m |
|---|---|---|---|
| ratio cap ≤ 5 binds on | 7 % | 23 % | 29 % |
| `D ≤ θ_a D0` (tortuosity ≥ 1) would bind on | 0.5 % | 1.5 % | 2.4 % |

Some bound is needed. Without one, the corrected formula exceeds D0 on 0.1 % of land (ROSETTA), and on up to 11 % of dry land with the Gupta et al. maps. This PR keeps the ratio cap.

## Tests

- The test that restated the old formula now checks that the water left at `θ_a100` sits at ψ = −1 m.
- `air_filled_porosity_100cm` has its own unit test. The function floors the result at `eps(FT)`, for Brooks–Corey soils that are still saturated at −1 m.
- Ran locally:
  - `co2_parameterizations`
  - `biogeochemistry_module`
  - `saturation_stability_test`
  - `soil_energy_hydrology_biogeochemistry`
  - `diagnostics/compute_methods`
  - `aqua`

title: Fix θ_a100: air-filled porosity at -100 cm, not the water content

body:
## Summary

1. **Depth limit on decomposition** (Koven et al. 2013, Biogeosciences 10:7109, Eq. 7).
   - The DAMM microbial source is multiplied by `exp(-depth / z_τ)`, with the new parameter
     `soilCO2_decomposition_efolding_depth` z_τ = 0.5 m.
   - `soilCO2_reference_rate` goes from 6.7e-7 to 1.273e-6 (×1.9), so global heterotrophic
     respiration (Rh) at SoilGrids SOC stays about the same. This re-tunes the value set in #1968.
2. **Soil carbon spin-up.**
   - `Simulations.spin_up_carbon_pools!(sim, t; soil_carbon = true)` sets each soil layer's SOC to
     the value at which its respiration over the spin-up period balances its litter input. It
     samples the respiration hourly at 41 candidate SOC values, from 10⁻³ to 100 kg C m⁻³; a
     layer without a balance below 100 keeps its SOC.
   - The opt-LAI long run uses it in its second spin-up year, so its scored year starts from SOC in
     equilibrium with the model's own litter, not from SoilGrids.

Both are documented on the DAMM model page.

## Why

Against CarbonTracker CT2022, the SH NEE seasonal cycle is 3.8–4.8× CT's, and Australia is a strong
source (+0.7 to +1.3 g C m⁻² d⁻¹). GPP is fine (it matches GOSIF in every SH region); ER is the
problem:
- **Unbalanced SOC:** in drylands, SoilGrids SOC is far out of balance with the model's litter
  (Australia: Rh 2.1 against litter 0.5 g C m⁻² d⁻¹).
- **Rh from the wrong depth:** in Australia, 79% of Rh comes from below 0.3 m, where the soil is
  wet and aseasonal.

In an independent study by the PR author, the Koven-style depth limit also gave better agreement
with soil-CO₂ profiles at NEON sites.

## Results

Global opt-LAI long runs, scored as the leaderboard (CT2022 NEE, g C m⁻² d⁻¹, 2010-03..2011-02):

| run | lb NEE RMSE | seasonal-cycle RMSE | SH NEE amp / CT | Australia NEE bias | NH NEE amp (CT 1.86) | global mean NEE (CT −0.07) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 0.756 | 0.802 | 3.78 | +1.28 | 1.80 | +0.05 |
| depth limit only | 0.660 | 0.765 | 3.18 | +0.51 | 1.64 | −0.02 |
| spin-up only | 0.532 | 0.723 | 3.50 | −0.06 | 1.81 | −0.31 |
| **this PR** | **0.425** | **0.708** | **2.96** | −0.11 | 1.68 | −0.16 |
| this PR with z_τ = 1 m, ×1.48 | 0.457 | 0.708 | 3.19 | −0.09 | 1.72 | −0.21 |

- **Reproduced:** this PR's Buildkite opt-LAI long run (build 5185) matches the "this PR" row within
  5e-5 on every leaderboard RMSE. The review changes (cebc34e3e) leave the results unchanged.
- **Other fluxes:** GPP and the energy fluxes are unchanged, and ER RMSE falls 2%.
- **Timing:** the NH peak-uptake month moves from June to July, as in CT.
- **Prescribed LAI:** only the depth limit applies; NEE RMSE goes 0.914 → 0.888.

## Caveats

- **The equilibrium leaves a sink** (global NEE −0.16 vs CT −0.07). DAMM saturates in cold or dry
  topsoil, so some layers cannot respire their litter at any SOC below 100 kg C m⁻³ and keep
  accumulating. This PR does not address it.
- **Equilibrium SOC differs from SoilGrids:**
  - top metre: below it (12.7 vs 16.0 kg C m⁻² globally; Australia 5.5 vs 19.4);
  - below 2 m: above it (5.6 vs 1.0).
- **z_τ is debated.** CLM5 weakened its depth limit, and CLM6 uses 10 m; 0.5 m is Koven 2013's
  ¹⁴C-based value.
- **Short spin-up:** the equilibrium covers one ERA5 year, not a pre-industrial spin-up.
- **Prescribed-LAI long run:** it also changes, but it needs the `Run long runs` label.

## Tests

- **Unit tests:** the depth factor, and the equilibrium solver (a known root on a saturating curve,
  the linear range, layers without litter, saturated layers).
- **Integrated test** on a coarse global land model: the solved SOC balances the litter within 2%,
  and `soil_carbon = true` leaves SOC finite and non-negative.

title: Slow DAMM decomposition with depth, and spin up soil carbon in the opt-LAI long run

body:
Two problems kept the soil O₂ volumetric fraction `so2` far above the atmospheric 0.21. In the global long run it reached 2–34, at depth and near the surface in cold regions.

**1. Initial conditions.** `set_soilco2_initial_conditions!` initialized O₂ with the effective porosity of CO₂, `θ_a + β_CO₂ θ_l`, instead of O₂'s, `θ_a + β_O₂ θ_l`. CO₂ is about 30 times more soluble in water than O₂. So wherever pores held water or ice, the soil air started with far more O₂ than the atmosphere has. The ERA5-Land, atmosphere-and-parameters and FLUXNET initializers set a uniform 0.08 kg O₂ m⁻³, which has the same problem.

All initializers now start CO₂ and O₂ from the soil state, each gas with its own effective porosity. The FLUXNET one keeps its own SOC.

**2. Pores that fill during a run.** When water or ice filled pores, the O₂ of the layer stayed put while its effective porosity shrank. So `so2` rose, about 12-fold when soil at θ_l = 0.25 saturates. It then stayed high, since gas barely diffuses through full pores.

O₂ above the atmospheric concentration is now released over one hour. The atmospheric concentration is taken at the air temperature, as in the top boundary condition. The column total is kept as a flux to the atmosphere, `o2_release_flux`, so O₂ mass is conserved.

`so2` before and after:

| case | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| initialization, pores full of ice (z = −0.15 m) | 7.33 | 0.200 |
| initialization, pores full of water (z = −0.75 m) | 4.75 | 0.163 |
| initialization from atmosphere and parameters, column maximum | 0.409 | 0.203 |
| soil below 0.5 m saturating, two days later (z = −1.05 m) | 2.58 | 0.210 |

In the initialization rows, "after" equals the intended profile, 0.21 · exp(z ln(0.21/0.15)).

The release is one-sided, so layers that diffusion reaches slowly settle at the concentration of the warmest air. With air at 263 ± 10 K over soil at 275 K, the daily mean `so2` at 2 m after 30 days is 0.211 instead of 0.219.

Tests:
- The initializers are tested in `soil_energy_hydrology_biogeochemistry.jl`, `soil_canopy_lsm.jl` and `full_land.jl`. Each check fails before the fix. No test covers the ERA5-Land initializer.
- The release is tested in `co2_parameterizations.jl` and `saturation_stability_test.jl`.
